rhyl.snapshot: Rhyl sits on the Denbighshire coast where full fibre is going in fast and the telecoms trade splits two ways. Build contractors and structured-cabling firms run fleets of engineers and buy on trade accounts, while ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. A workwear supplier here kits both, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.
rhyl.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Denbighshire
s1loc: Rhyl and the wider Denbighshire coast are deep in a full-fibre build. Openreach has reached roughly 95 per cent of properties across the town and pushed its network out through Kinmel Bay, Rhuddlan and along the coast toward Prestatyn, and the Welsh alt-net Ogi is building fibre across North Wales alongside it. The major mobile networks keep upgrading on top, and Project Gigabit work reaches the harder rural addresses inland. That mix means engineers and civils crews are working through the town's streets, cabinets and customer premises week in, week out, from the seafront estates to the newer developments behind the promenade.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a steady commercial scene. Structured-cabling and CCTV installers wire offices, schools and trade units across Tir Llwyd Industrial Estate at Kinmel Bay and the Colomendy Industrial Estate over toward Denbigh, running Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre for multi-site businesses along the A55 corridor. Hotels, holiday parks and retail along the Rhyl front need cabling, access control and camera systems too, so a long tail of independent broadband, network and CCTV firms takes on work across the town for homes and businesses alike.
